\begin{table}[t]\centering\footnotesize
\caption{\textbf{Out-of-sample multi-view clustering.} Inductive AMI on held-out points, mean$\pm$std over the 19 dataset means (10 seeds each, 190 cells per method). Inductive AMI clusters the \emph{training} embedding with $k$-means and applies that clustering to the extended test embedding, so it fails unless the extension lands unseen points in the same coordinate frame. All diffusion methods share one kernel, one truncated-SVD embedding at $k=\lvert C\rvert$ components, and one Nystr\"om extension obtained by writing each operator as $\mathbf W=\sum_v \mathbf P_v \mathbf S_v$ and substituting the test-to-train transition for the leftmost factor. $^{*}$ inside the MDT operator space (Sec.~3.5); a win over these concerns trajectory choice, not the framework. $^{\S}$ inductive by construction, no Nystr\"om step. PRR is Eq.~\ref{eq:prr} against MDT-\textsc{Rand} as a ratio of means. \emph{W--L} counts datasets on which MDT-\textsc{Direct} beats / loses to that row; $p_{\mathrm{H}}$ is a Holm-corrected exact sign test over the 16-comparison family. $^{\ddagger}$ ours, not a variant of the paper. $^{\dagger}$ per-cell maximum over the six MDT variants; it uses test labels, so it is an upper bound rather than a method, and its sign test is degenerate by construction. $^{\P}$ concatenation projected to $k$ dimensions, so that the control has the same representational budget as the diffusion arms.}

\begin{table}[t]\centering\footnotesize
\caption{\textbf{Kernel ablation.} Inductive AMI, 19 datasets $\times$ 5 seeds, paired cell for cell. \emph{Scale-inv.} is $\exp(-d^2/2\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma$ a median pairwise distance on standardised views: dimensionless, hence invariant to rescaling a view. \emph{Reference} reproduces \texttt{benchmarks/utilities.get\_kernel\_matrix} of the MDT reference repository: $\exp(-d^2/\mathit{bw})$ with $\mathit{bw}=\max_i\min_{j\neq i} d_{ij}$ on raw views. That divides a squared distance by a distance, so it is not scale invariant and on views with large absolute scale every off-diagonal weight underflows and the row-normalised operator becomes the identity (mean diagonal $1.000$ on MSRC-v5 view~1, $0.997$ on Handwritten view~1, $0.917$ on Yale view~1); estimating the bandwidth on training rows only is not the cause, train and full-data bandwidths agreeing to 1--3\%. Every diffusion arm degrades and the ordering does not survive (Spearman $\rho = +0.525$), so the main result is kernel-conditional.}

\begin{table}[t]\centering\scriptsize
\caption{\textbf{Verified differences between the paper and its reference implementation.} Each was confirmed in the source or empirically. The last two rows are defects rather than divergences.}
\label{tab:discrepancies}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.30\linewidth} p{0.22\linewidth} p{0.42\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
Item & Location & Consequence\\
\midrule
Singular entropy normalised by the $L_2$ norm, not $L_1$ & \texttt{utilities/entropy.py} & Eq.~18 is not the entropy of a distribution. Shifts the selected diffusion time on 4/4 shipped datasets (MSRC 12 vs 1, Yale 8 vs 10, 100Leaves 5 vs 7, Caltech101-7 10 vs 17).\\[2pt]
Kernel differs from the paper in two places & \texttt{benchmarks/utilities.py} & Paper: $\exp(-d/2\sigma^2)$. Code: $\exp(-d^2/\mathit{bw})$. Squared distance, and $\mathit{bw}$ in place of $2\sigma^2$.\\[2pt]
$k$-NN count is $\lfloor\log N\rfloor$ & \texttt{benchmarks/utilities.py} & Paper states $\lceil\log N\rceil$.\\[2pt]
$Q_X$ sign is internally inconsistent & paper Eq.~17 vs 19 & Eq.~17 maximises $Q$; Eq.~19 defines $Q_X$ as a sum of negative log-probabilities. The code minimises it.\\[2pt]
$Q_{CH}$ scored on transition matrices, not data views & \texttt{mdt/mdt\_direct.py} & Paper writes $CH(\mathbf X_v, C)$. Load-bearing: scoring on views instead drops MDT-\textsc{Direct} from $0.417$ to $0.356$.\\[2pt]
MDT-\textsc{Bsc} grows the product on the opposite side & \texttt{mdt/\_mdt\_tree\_utils.py} & \texttt{parent.path\_operator @ op} yields $\mathbf W_1\cdots\mathbf W_d$, reversing Def.~1. Same reachable set, different greedy prefix.\\[2pt]
MDT-\textsc{Cvx-Rand} is not Dirichlet & \texttt{mdt/random\_mdt.py} & Normalised i.i.d.\ uniforms concentrate near the simplex centre, i.e.\ nearer the uniform mean than a Dirichlet draw.\\[2pt]
GCCA and MVSC implemented but unreported, and fed operators & \texttt{competitors/} & Both receive the $n\times n$ transition matrices as ``views''. On raw views with a variance rank cut, GCCA rises from $\approx 0.03$ to $\approx 0.68$ AMI on MSRC-v5.\\[2pt]
\textbf{L-Isolet: two of its three views are identical} & \texttt{benchmarks/isolet\_lindenbaum.py} & $K_1$ and $K_2$ are written into one buffer and appended by reference, so the first is overwritten. Verified \texttt{allclose(view1,view2)}. The published L-Isolet has two distinct views, not three.\\[2pt]
PCA and min-max fitted before the split & \texttt{benchmarks/mnist\_*.py}, \texttt{olivetti.py} & Harmless transductively; leaks under any out-of-sample protocol.\\[2pt]
Unseeded global RNG in \texttt{random\_mdt} & \texttt{mdt/random\_mdt.py} & Single MDT-\textsc{Rand} runs are not reproducible.\\[2pt]
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
